name: First Lunar Pathloss Radio Map Prediction Challenge

units.tx: one-hot uint8 mask of the transmitter pixel

simulation.rx_sampling: triangle centroids of a copy of the terrain mesh translated +1 m in z, linearly interpolated (scipy griddata) onto a regular 256x256 grid, then flipud. RX follows the terrain contour; it is not a flat plane.
simulation.tx_antenna: PlanarArray 1x1, pattern='iso', polarization='V', one transmitter per tile
simulation.rx_antenna: none modeled; isotropic probe at each sample point
simulation.diffraction_note: RadioMapSolver in Sionna 1.1.0 exposes no diffraction parameter, so diffraction is absent by construction rather than switched off.
simulation.monte_carlo: Per-tile averaging (np.nanmean) over incrementing solver seeds to resolve unsampled cells: up to 15 generation attempts targeting <1000 NaN cells of 65536, then up to 60 refinement attempts from seed 30 targeting <=500, with a diminishing-returns cutoff.

gap_filling.pipeline: (1) scipy griddata linear interpolation from mesh centroids onto the regular 256x256 grid; (2) Monte Carlo averaging across solver seeds to reduce unresolved cells; (3) a final fill for cells still missing.
gap_filling.415: linear interpolation; filled pixels take continuous values and are not marked.
gap_filling.58: static fill at 145.0 dB pathloss. 5.8 GHz left much larger contiguous voids, which is why a static value was used instead of interpolation.

split.stratified_by: tx count group (multi=51 TX, single=1 TX)
split.note: Terrains are split three ways. A terrain carrying 51 transmitters contributes 51 samples that share one heightmap, so splitting at the sample level would leak terrain between train and val/test.

notes: Pathloss is the positive convention, -10*log10(path_gain), obtained from the raw simulation arrays as 30 - stored_value. The raw arrays hold watt_to_dbm(path_gain), i.e. a dBm conversion applied to a unitless ratio, so they are neither RSS nor path gain; the offset removes that bookkeeping artifact.
Pathloss here is independent of transmit power. The simulation used a fixed 20 dBm isotropic transmitter, so RSS in dBm can be recovered as 20 - pathloss_dB.
Heightmaps are stored once per terrain and referenced by index.csv; terrains carrying 51 TX share a single heightmap across their 51 samples.
Heightmaps are given in metres above each tile's own minimum elevation.

5.8 GHz maps contain a static fill of exactly 145.0 dB in cells the ray tracer could not resolve -- about 11.4% of all 5.8 GHz pixels, and a majority of a few individual maps. These are placeholders, not simulated values, and they are EXCLUDED from scoring -- the metric is RMSE over valid (ray-traced) pixels only.

storage.layout: consolidated arrays, one file per split per field
storage.file_names: <split>_<field>.npy at the archive root, e.g. train_pl415.npy; a nested <split>/<field>.npy build is also recognised by the loader
storage.row_order: row i of <split>_pl<band>.npy and <split>_mask<band>.npy is row i of <split>_index.csv
storage.heightmaps: deduplicated -- one row per terrain; index.csv column hm_row indexes <split>_hm.npy
storage.tx: not stored -- rebuild from index.csv: tx = np.zeros((256,256), np.float32); tx[tx_row, tx_col] = 1.0
storage.reading: open arrays with mmap_mode='r'; train targets are 3.4 GB per band

evaluation.scored_pixels: valid only -- pixels where the validity mask is 1
evaluation.submission: full 256x256 maps; the mask is applied by the organizers at scoring time, so entrants never need the test masks
